conditions_of_satisfaction: The actual source of the reported cent-off discrepancy is identified and a targeted fix is proposed
The existing test suite continues to pass (all tests in tests/test_utils.py, including test_round_money_half_up)
scope_exclusions: Does not swap round_money to bare round() — that change is not included in this commitment
parsed.concern: The swap to bare round() would break three existing tests that explicitly verify half-up rounding (test_round_money_half_up: 2.675→2.68, 1.005→1.01, 0.125→0.13). The test file even comments: 'a naive swap to bare round() would break here.' Python's built-in round() uses banker's rounding (half-to-even), so these cases would return 2.67, 1.00, and 0.12 respectively — the opposite direction from the expected fix. The +1e-9 nudge is intentional documented behavior for half-up rounding, not a bug. If monthly totals are coming out a cent off, the culprit is more likely in the summation or tax/rate calculation logic rather than in round_money itself. I can investigate the actual source of the discrepancy and propose a targeted fix without regressing the rounding semantics the tests rely on.
